token.description: The auth token used to authenticate with Sanity. May be sourced from the `SANITY_TOKEN` environment variable instead of via this attribute.

allow_credentials.description: Indicates whether the origin is allowed to send credentials (e.g. a session cookie or an authorization token). Defaults to `true`.

id.description: The unique ID for the CORS origin.

origin.description: The origin you want to allow traffic from, stating explicitly the protocol, host name and port. Wildcards (`*`) are allowed. Use the following format: `protocol://host:port`.

project.description: The ID of the project that the CORS origin belongs to.

block.description: Provides a CORS origin to a Sanity project. A CORS origin is a host that can connect to the Sanity Project API.

acl_mode.description: The ACL mode for the data. Valid options are `public` and `private`.

project.description: The ID of the project that the dataset belongs to.

block.description: Provides a dataset to a Sanity project. A dataset is like a database for your content, and you manage its contents with a studio and query it with GROQ or GraphQL.

activity_feed_enabled.description: Indicates whether the [activity feed](https://www.sanity.io/docs/activity-feed) is enabled. Defaults to `true`.

color.description: The hex value for the project color. This is the color of the project icon at https://sanity.io/manage.

disabled_by_user.description: Indicates whether the project is archived. Defaults to `false`.

id.description: The project ID, which you can find at the top of the project page in Sanity.

organization.description: The name of the organization that owns the project.

studio_host.description: The studio host URL. This attribute exhibits two unique behaviors that are important to note. First, once the studio host URL is set, it may not be changed. Changing this value will force a replacement. Second, when the studio host is set, Sanity will automatically create a CORS entry for the studio host URL. This means that it is not necessary for you to create a CORS entry, and you will get a conflict error if you do.

block.description: Provides a Sanity project. A project is the base resource for creating content, and the project may contain datasets, CORS origins, and tags.

id.description: The unique token ID generated by Sanity.

key.description: The token value. This value can be used for making authenticated requests against the API with the permissions indicated by the role name.

label.description: A descriptive label for the token.

project.description: The project ID, which you can find at the top of the project page in Sanity.

role_name.description: The role name that indicates which permissions are assigned to the token. For a free account, valid values are `viewer`, `editor`, and `deploy-studio`.

block.description: Provides a Sanity project token. The token key is a sensitive value that can be used to make authenticated requests against the Sanity HTTP API.

disabled_by_user.description: Indicates whether the project is archived.

id.description: The project ID, which you can find at the top of the project page in Sanity.

organization.description: The name of the organization that owns the project.

block.description: Gets a Sanity project by its ID. A project is the base resource for creating content, and the project may contain datasets, CORS origins, and tags.
